---
title: "Washington, DC as a Rail Hub"
author: "Jeremy Handy"
date: "2026-10-23"
output: html_document
---

## Map instructions and context

The red-outlined blue marker identifies Washington, DC, the origin market being examined. The other markers represent destination markets for Washington, DC's short-haul flights in the 2019 BTS DB1B Coupon data. Marker colors indicate the number of passengers traveling from Washington, DC to each destination; hover over a destination for a quick summary and click a marker for its popup.

This map uses the revised 2026 city-market analysis. City-market names and representative coordinates come from the project's derived data. These points are representative locations, not exact boundaries or geographic centroids of the BTS city markets.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(
  root.dir = "/Users/jeremyhandy/Trains_for_planes_cars/Trains_for_planes_2026"
)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(stringr)
library(scales)

# Keep map layers in latitude/longitude for web mapping.
mapview::mapviewOptions(
  basemaps = "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas"
)

# Paths are relative to the project root.
hub_file <- "data/Cities_as_rail_hubs_2026.csv"
roads_file <- "data/roads/tl_2016_us_primaryroads.shp"

hub_data <- read_csv(hub_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    Sum_of_Passengers = parse_number(as.character(Sum_of_Passengers)),
    Origin_Rank = as.integer(Origin_Rank),
    Destination_Rank = as.integer(Destination_Rank)
  )

# Select Washington, DC using the city-market name rather than relying only on rank.
dc_data <- hub_data %>%
  filter(Origin_City_Market == "Washington, DC (Metropolitan Area)")

if (nrow(dc_data) == 0) {
  stop("No Washington, DC rows were found in data/Cities_as_rail_hubs_2026.csv.")
}

# The same origin coordinates repeat across Washington, DC's destination rows.
dc_origin <- dc_data %>%
  distinct(Origin_City_Market, OriginLat, OriginLon, Origin_Rank)

dc_destinations <- dc_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(DestLat),
    !is.na(DestLon),
    !is.na(Sum_of_Passengers)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Destination_Rank) %>%
  transmute(
    Destination_City_Market = Dest_City_Market,
    `Sum of Passengers` = Sum_of_Passengers,
    `Destination Rank` = Destination_Rank,
    DestLat,
    DestLon,
    Distance
  )

if (nrow(dc_destinations) == 0) {
  stop("Washington, DC was found, but no destination rows have usable coordinates and passenger counts.")
}

# Convert origin and destination tables to point layers.
dc_origin_sf <- st_as_sf(
  dc_origin,
  coords = c("OriginLon", "OriginLat"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)
dc_origin_sf$Origin_Label <- "Origin"

dc_destinations_sf <- st_as_sf(
  dc_destinations,
  coords = c("DestLon", "DestLat"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

dc_destinations_sf$Passenger_Band <- cut(
  dc_destinations_sf[["Sum of Passengers"]],
  breaks = c(-Inf, 100000,200000, Inf),
  labels = c(
    "0–100,000",
    "100,001-200,000",
    "200,001 or more"
  ),
  include.lowest = TRUE,
  ordered_result = TRUE
)

dc_destinations_sf$Rank_Label <- paste(
  "Destination Rank",
  dc_destinations_sf[["Destination Rank"]]
)
dc_destinations_popup <- dc_destinations_sf %>%
  select(
    Destination_City_Market,
    `Sum of Passengers`,
    Passenger_Band,
    Rank_Label,
    DestLat,
    DestLon,
    Distance
)

# Read and transform roads to the same CRS as the map points.
roads <- st_read(roads_file, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

# Crop roads to the extent of Washington, DC and its listed destinations, with padding.
# This keeps the HTML output smaller than embedding the entire national road layer.
# Combine the origin and destination point geometries
all_points <- st_sfc(
  c(
    st_geometry(dc_origin_sf),
    st_geometry(dc_destinations_sf)
  ),
  crs = 4326
)

# Calculate the bounding box around all points
point_bbox <- st_bbox(all_points)
padding_lon <- 2
padding_lat <- 1.5

map_bbox <- st_bbox(
  c(
    xmin = max(-125, point_bbox["xmin"] - padding_lon),
    ymin = max(24, point_bbox["ymin"] - padding_lat),
    xmax = min(-66, point_bbox["xmax"] + padding_lon),
    ymax = min(50, point_bbox["ymax"] + padding_lat)
  ),
  crs = st_crs(4326)
)

roads_local <- st_crop(roads, map_bbox)
```

## Visualization

```{r map, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
destination_map <- mapview(
  dc_destinations_popup,
  zcol = "Passenger_Band",
col.regions = c(
  "0–100,000" = "#fff7bc",
  "100,001–200,000" = "#fec44f",
  "200,001 or more" = "#cc4c02"
  ),
  layer.name = "Passengers from Washington, DC",
  popup = TRUE,
  legend = TRUE,
  label = "Rank_Label"
)
roads_map <- mapview(
  roads_local,
  color = "#555555",
  lwd = 1,
  alpha.regions = 0,
  legend = FALSE,
  layer.name = "U.S. primary roads"
)
origin_map <- mapview(
  dc_origin_sf,
  color = "#d73027",
  col.regions = "#1769aa",
  cex = 8,
  layer.name = "Washington, DC origin market",
  popup = TRUE,
  legend = FALSE,
  label = "Origin_Label"
)

roads_map + destination_map + origin_map
```

## 2016 U.S. Primary Roads Notes

- The maps use the 2016 U.S. Primary Roads National Shapefile from the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line program. The dataset represents primary roads, generally limited-access highways, and is used as a visual reference layer rather than as a complete road network.

- The dataset is listed under the CC0 1.0 public-domain dedication. It has been cropped to the map area for visualization.

- Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2016 TIGER/Line Primary Roads. https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/tiger-line-shapefile-2016-nation-u-s-primary-roads-national-shapefile
